# WO-611: Registry health re-checks search access and flags searchable brokers without a parser
Status: queued (in-house)
Vendor: claude
Agent: qa-security (Marcus Webb)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: tests
Severity: MEDIUM
Target release: 0.4
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
The only broker marked `search_access: open` loaded with a plain fetch on 2026-11-07 and returned HTTP 403 with a challenge page four days later. Nothing in the weekly health check notices that drift, and nothing flags the 22 brokers that have `search_url_pattern` but no `search:` spec (they can never produce a listing; see WO-601).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. `tools/registry_health.py` gains a search check: for brokers with `search_access` open, one polite GET of the search URL built from a FAKE person (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL), through NetPolicy; a challenge or 4xx marks the entry "search access drifted".
2. A static check (no network) lists brokers with `search_url_pattern` and no `search.result_selector`, and brokers whose `search_url_checked` is older than 30 days.
3. The report separates "broken opt-out" (non-zero exit, as today) from "search drift" (warning, non-zero only with `--strict`).
4. Tests: fake httpx transport returning 403/challenge -> drift; static check on a fake registry; no real network in tests.

## Allowed paths
- `tools/registry_health.py`
- `tests/test_registry_health.py`

## Out of scope / do not touch
Any challenge handling; real person data (fake person only).

## Required checks
- `.venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_registry_health.py`
- `.venv/bin/ruff check src tests`

## Check-in plan
Handoff note; CI weekly job picks it up unchanged.
